page: Amazon Web Services c8a.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single dedicated x86_64 physical core running on an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 2.0 GB of DDR5 operating at 6 GHz, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 4 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), SHA-NI, and VAES. There is no local instance storage attached, and baseline network throughput is set to 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the high-clocked dedicated single core. Synthetic CPU evaluation via stress-ng places single-core performance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems, matched by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. Memory bandwidth achieves moderate results on uncached large blocks, with read throughput of 47.05 GB/s and write throughput of 33.96 GB/s. However, aggregate multi-threaded capabilities, overall PassMark scores, and Redis operations register in lower benchmark tiers due to the strict physical limitation of a single core and 2.0 GB of RAM.

Cost efficiency is focused on lightweight compute-centric tasks where full core isolation is required without paying for multi-core density. The primary tradeoff lies in low memory capacity and the absence of attached NVMe storage, which restricts data caching and IO-heavy persistence. The c8a.medium is best matched with lightweight batch processing, single-threaded computational routines, entry-level web serving, microservices, and dedicated CI/CD build workers.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.medium is a compute-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro system, powered by a dedicated 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 1 physical core and 1 vCPU. It is equipped with 2.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 6 GHz, baseline network performance of 1 Gbps, and no local NVMe storage. Hardware feature support includes AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside VAES and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core compute and compression performance, offset by entry-level multi-core and overall throughput metrics bounded by the single-core footprint. The server provides a cost-effective environment for isolated single-threaded workloads, lightweight web serving, microservices, and simple batch processing routines.
